newsitem.title: FINLAND: TWO FINNISH MINISTERS CRITICAL OF ERM LINK - MEDIA.
newsitem.headline: TWO FINNISH MINISTERS CRITICAL OF ERM LINK - MEDIA.

text.p: Culture Minister Claes Andersson, chairman of the Leftist Alliance, and second Finance Minister Arja Alho voiced criticism over the weekend of linking the markka to the ERM, Finnish media reported.
Andersson opposes linking the markka to the Exchange Rate Mechanism, Finnish News Agency (STT) said on Saturday.
The STT quoted Andersson as saying ERM involves many risks and that a decision to link the markka to ERM would be a political issue without economic grounds.
It was the first time his party, the second smallest in Paavo Lipponen's left-right-green coalition, has given a direct view on ERM although many party members have voiced critical opinions.
The biggest risk with ERM is if the Finnish economy were hit and the Bank of Finland had to defend the currency by raising interest rates, he was quoted as saying.
Another problem is that the markka is too strong, he said.
Finnish local newspaper Karjalainen on Sunday reported that second Finance Minister Arja Alho saw reasons to hold off on a decision on ERM, citing worrying signals from other ERM countries.
However, she also said the Finnish economy is so stable that Finland would not have any "terribly big problem" in linking the markka tomorrow or within months.

Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said three weeks ago that the time is ripe for a decision on whether or not to join the ERM, and financial market operators expect a link to happen any time before or after October 20 local elections.
